summary: The long shot for the top: {donor} tells you that you can win {the top office}, and the first polls agree.
realLife: One life: Donors expected him to win the 2016 nomination. By September 2015 he polled under one percent, quit, and urged other candidates to quit to stop Trump. Another: He quit the 2016 race after New Hampshire and endorsed Trump weeks later. Another: Challenging Trump in 2019, he debated a cardboard cutout of him when South Carolina's party skipped its primary, and quit within months. Another: He ran against the president he had served, raised little, withdrew in October 2023, and endorsed no one.
